## Appearance

He is a short, fat, bald man with a round face, prominent blue eyes, and a small fringe of hair around his ears. He is sensitive about his bald head. Under his wife's household care, he keeps his face neatly shaved and his hair carefully trimmed, wearing neatly patched and brushed clothes.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c1 P21](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0021), [v2 c1 P22](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0022), [v2 c25 P46](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0046)_

## Personality

He is an outspoken, crusty, and opinionated individual who prided himself on telling the disagreeable part of the plain truth. Though considered an odd crank by his neighbors, he possesses a kind and sociable nature once understood. He has a quick temper when angered, but he can quickly become subdued, forgive mistakes, and hold no hard feelings. He enjoys pipe smoking, eating cake, and sharing friendly chats.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P22](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0022), [v2 c1 P23](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0023), [v2 c1 P24](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0024), [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c3 P29](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0029), [v2 c3 P35](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0035), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049), [v2 c9 P5](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0005), [v2 c9 P6](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0006), [v2 c9 P9](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0009), [v2 c20 P8](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0008), [v2 c30 P2](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0002)_

## History

After moving to Avonlea from New Brunswick, Mr. Harrison quickly earned a reputation as an eccentric bachelor who kept house for himself and owned a foul-mouthed parrot named Ginger. He got into a heated dispute with Anne Shirley over her Jersey cow breaking into his oatfield, but after Anne accidentally sold his cow and confessed with a cake as a peace offering, the two became close friends. When a lightning strike killed Ginger, Anne came over to comfort him in his grief. Shortly afterward, his estranged wife Emily arrived in Avonlea and reconciled with him, transforming his untidy house into a clean, orderly home. Over time, Mr. Harrison settled comfortably into community life, regularly attending church, supporting the minister's salary, and offering candid feedback on Anne's writing projects.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P10](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0010), [v2 c1 P15](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0015), [v2 c2 P35](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0035), [v2 c3 P8](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0008), [v2 c3 P28](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0028), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c24 P41](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0041), [v2 c24 P43](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0043), [v2 c25 P10](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0010), [v2 c25 P25](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0025), [v2 c25 P46](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0046), [v2 c25 P60](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0060), [v2 c28 P8](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0008), [v3 c11 P50](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0050), [v3 c12 P39](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0039), [v3 c12 P41](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0041)_

## Background by volume

- Moved from New Brunswick to Avonlea, buying Robert Bell's farm  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- Had a brother who was a sailor and gave him a parrot  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006), [v2 c3 P38](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0038)</sub>
- Separated from his wife Emily before her arrival in Avonlea  <sub>[v2 c25 P25](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0025), [v2 c25 P43](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0043), [v2 c25 P60](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0060)</sub>

## Quotes

> I can't help speaking out just what I think and folks must take me as they find me.  <sub>[v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023)</sub>

> I'm a crusty, lonesome, crabbed old chap, but there's something about that little girl makes me feel young again . . . and it's such a pleasant sensation I'd like to have it repeated once in a while.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

> So I do . . . so I do . . . but my approval doesn't go as deep as my pocket, Anne.  <sub>[v2 c6 P59](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0059)</sub>

> Changes ain't totally pleasant but they're excellent things. Two years is about long enough for things to stay exactly the same.  <sub>[v2 c30 P1](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0001)</sub>

> If I had to have villains at all, I'd give them a chance, Anne—I'd give them a chance.  <sub>[v3 c12 P74](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0074)</sub>
